instruction:
Compare the products written for the same Rubisco-associated reaction across module annotations. Return all qualifying reaction–module pairs for reactions whose product sets differ across modules.

Use the annotations observed on 12 September 2026, with no publication-year filter. R, M, and C identifiers identify reactions, modules (functional units), and compounds, respectively.

Eligible reactions are all reaction IDs in the full ALL_REAC field of enzyme EC 4.1.1.39, including entries marked other. The module scope is all modules in its official direct enzyme-to-module links, without filtering by module name or organism. Coverage must include each linked module in full. A module line is in scope only when its REACTION field contains an exact match to an eligible reaction ID. A comma-separated reaction ID list applies the line to each listed reaction.

A qualifying line explicitly consumes D-ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate (C01182). Read -> or => from left to right, and <- or <= from right to left. For <-> or <=>, use the direction consuming C01182 if it appears on exactly one side. C01182 on both sides leaves consumption unresolved. Do not reverse a one-way arrow to make a line qualify. Each product set contains only the compound IDs explicitly written on that line's product side. Ignore coefficients and compound order; deduplicate IDs.

The requested reactions have at least two distinct product sets across different linked modules, compared within the same reaction ID. Return all qualifying module rows for each retained reaction, including rows that share a product set. Exclude reactions represented in only one qualifying module or with identical product sets throughout.

No products may be added from a generic reaction entry's EQUATION or from other module lines. This comparison concerns written annotations, not complete chemical stoichiometry, biological absence, or organism phenotype.

Repeated qualifying lines for the same reaction–module pair collapse to one row when their product sets agree; conflicting sets are unresolved. A complete module with no matching REACTION line contributes no row. If a required record is incomplete, or a matching line's direction or product set is unresolved, report the unresolved issue instead of a table or NONE.
output_format: Return a pipe-separated table with the header REACTION_ID|MODULE_ID|PRODUCT_IDS. Include every qualifying pair, with one row per distinct (REACTION_ID, MODULE_ID). Sort rows by REACTION_ID ascending, then MODULE_ID ascending. Within PRODUCT_IDS, list the unique compound IDs in ascending order, separated by commas without spaces. Do not include commentary or additional columns in a completed answer. If the complete, resolved comparison yields no qualifying pairs, return only NONE, without a header. Incomplete or unresolved research must not be represented by NONE or a partial table.
